problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize F(x)=max_{i<m} f_i(x) over the closed ball B(x0,R). Every component is convex on this ball, so F is convex there; F need not be differentiable.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Finite-maximum optimization with m≥2 smooth components. The objective is a maximum, rather than a finite sum.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query selects an index i and point x. For x∈B(x0,R), the reply contains the exact component gradient ∇f_i(x), independently of history and oracle seed. Each component query costs one oracle call; obtaining all components at one point costs m calls.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothFiniteMaximum.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace, Convergence

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same component query also returns the exact value f_i(x). Oracle replies outside the ball have no specified mathematical guarantee.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure. No dimension-dependent restriction is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: On B(x0,R), every component is differentiable, satisfies ‖∇f_i(x)‖≤G, and has L-Lipschitz gradient. A constrained minimizer xstar exists in the ball. These assumptions are required only on the ball. E, m, G, L, R, ε, δ, and x0 are public; component functions and xstar are hidden. Parameters satisfy G,R,ε>0, L≥0, and 0<δ<1.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The measurable output x must satisfy F(x)−F(xstar)≤ε with probability at least 1−δ.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The output belongs to B(x0,R) almost surely.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Almost-sure feasibility is required separately from the high-probability objective-gap guarantee.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: Success probability is at least 1−δ under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, with a fixed cap on the number of component-oracle calls.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothFiniteMaximum.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace, Convergence; supplied proved-result budgets

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Minimizing a finite maximum of convex, Lipschitz, smooth components over a Euclidean ball using exact component values and gradients is an established optimization formulation.
